messages:
Priya: Quick heads-up — converting an HF chat_template with inline Jinja comments is stripping assistant block content in Redwood render. Repro below.

Priya: Repro template (HF):
```
{% set user_name = "Sam" %}
{# assistant note: should stay #}
- role: system
  content: "You are helpful."
- role: user
  content: "Hello {{ user_name }}"
- role: assistant
  content: |
    Thanks for asking.
    {% if debug %}
    <!-- debug: {{ debug }} -->
    {% endif %}
```

Priya: After conversion to Redwood prompts we see the assistant content collapsed to an empty string or removed entirely: 
```
...
- role: assistant
  content: ""   # missing the multi-line reply
...
```

Priya: This only happens when there are inline Jinja comments `{# ... #}` or HTML comments inside the assistant block. Suspect preprocessor order (comment-stripper running before sentinel handling).

Alex: Which converter did you run? the legacy `tools/convert_chat.py` or the new preprocessor pipeline?

Priya: New pipeline (jinja pre-render -> yaml loader -> sentinel insertion). Using `--strip-comments` = true for the pre-render. Command: `python tools/convert_chat.py --template templates/greet.yaml --target redwood`.

Alex: hm. My guess: comment-stripper removes the `{# ... #}` tokens, then our sentinel inserter tries to detect the assistant block boundaries and gets confused because newlines changed. Can you paste the minimal string that goes into sentinel stage?

Priya: Minimal input to sentinel stage (after jinja render):
```
- role: assistant
  content: |
    Thanks for asking.
    <!-- debug: True -->

```

Priya: Notice the HTML comment survived and ends up on the same line as a blank line — our YAML loader treats it as comment and YAML->string conversion drops the block in some cases.

Jon: I saw a similar one where `<!-- -->` was preserved and later stripped by the YAML loader leaving trailing whitespace that made the downstream parser think the assistant block was empty. Two quick workarounds: 1) run sentinel replacement before comment stripping, or 2) wrap assistant multi-line content with `{% raw %}...{% endraw %}` during conversion so jinja doesn't touch inner comments.

Priya: `{% raw %}` helped locally, but breaks other templates that rely on nested jinja logic inside assistant messages. Also it's fragile to ask template authors to change their templates.

Alex: Agreed. We should change the pipeline: detect multi-line assistant blocks and mark them as verbatim during comment-strip step (i.e., skip comment stripping for those blocks). Add unit tests for at least three variants: `{# ... #}`, `<!-- ... -->`, and trailing comma/newline combos.

EvalBot: [regression-detect] EVAL_RUN_2026-03 flagged prompt mismatch for model "open-llama-3" on Jinja templates — assistant content dropped in 12% of prompts. Ticket created: #6743. :exclamation:

Priya: Good catch EvalBot. I'll open a PR with the pipeline change + tests and link #6743.

Alex: Also check special token insertion order: if we inject our sentinel like `<|assistant|>` after comment-strip, tokenizers (especially quantized ones) may map it to different token IDs. Confirm that sentinel insertion happens after any stripping and before tokenization.

Jon: I'll add a small fuzz test that runs templates through both orders and compares token counts and sentinel positions — catches subtle shifts due to comment removal.

Priya: Thanks. Will post PR link here once ready. :thumbsup:

Alex: sweet. Prioritize adding the three unit tests + one integration that runs on the quantized model config.

Priya: Ack, assigning work now and will follow up in #6743.
